answer: Galvanic soil-impedance attestation prevents Sybil attacks among autonomous agents in an olive grove. Nodes inject alternating currents through probes isolated by jade bushings and velvet dust collars, measuring mutual resistance tensors to verify discrete physical locations. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of sinking dedicated electrode arrays into the ground per identity. However, rainfall alters soil conductivity, occasionally causing legitimate agents to fail verification.
